highlights.content: ![BIOENGINEER.ORG](https://bioengineer.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/logo_sariyazi.png) ![Bioengineer.org](https://bioengineer.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/11/logo352-e1516556386659.png) # Explainable Cognitive Swarm Architecture Improves Multi-Agent Software Engineering Benchmark Accuracy ![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=80&r=g) ![Explainable Cognitive Swarm Architecture Improves Multi-Agent Software Engineering Benchmark Accuracy](https://bioengineer.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/stackrss-featured-12205-750x422-bio-e0a8d57ce30b-750w.webp) Explainable Cognitive Swarm Architecture Improves Multi-Agent Software Engineering Benchmark Accuracy Computer science researchers have introduced XCognitive SwarmNet, an explainable cognitive swarm framework designed to coordinate autonomous artificial intelligence agents across complex software development lifecycles and enterprise workflows. In controlled benchmark evaluations reported in Discover Artificial Intelligence, the multi-agent system completed evaluated tasks with an overall accuracy of 98.1 percent while attaining an explainability fidelity score of 97.5 percent. The experimental configuration also demonstrated a 27.4 percent reduction in overall execution time alongside a 22.8 percent relative reduction in computational resource consumption when compared against selected baseline multi-agent configurations. Beyond code generation accuracy, the framework achieved a measured software quality score of 96.8 percent and optimized business process workflow efficiency by 95.9 percent across standard test suites. The authors emphasize, however, that these performance indicators reflect controlled benchmark datasets rather than validated deployments within operational factory settings or safety-critical industrial environments. The rapid expansion of the Fourth Industrial Revolution has accelerated the incorporation of generative artificial intelligence and foundation models into enterprise software engineering and organizational management. Large language models frequently automate isolated engineering tasks, including software architecture design, requirement tracing, program synthesis, bug localization, and automated regression testing. Nevertheless, conventional multi-agent frameworks often encounter acute collaboration bottlenecks, opaque decision rationale, static communication patterns, and fragmented knowledge transfer across distinct project stages. Most prevailing implementations operate essentially as black-box systems, making it difficult for software architects, systems engineers, project managers, and governance auditors to inspect the causal reasoning behind autonomous recommendations. Furthermore, traditional multi-agent tools depend on isolated knowledge caches that cannot systematically adapt to fluid business rules or maintain traceable institutional memory across sequential projects. To overcome these collaborative constraints, the investigators structured XCognitive SwarmNet as an integrated control pipeline comprising seven coordinated components. Rather than running disconnected parallel modules, the framework routes tasks sequentially through the Context Intelligence Engine, Cognitive Swarm Layer, Collective Cognitive Memory, Explainable Decision DNA, Self-Evolving Agent Genome, Software and Business Digital Twin, and Autonomous Governance Engine. Initial task inputs, including software specifications, enterprise constraints, and delivery criteria, are ingested by the Context Intelligence Engine and converted into structured task profiles. The system initiates dynamic task decomposition whenever an input contains independently verifiable goals, sequential dependency chains, or distinct evaluation metrics. It advances visual intelligence and leads across a range of benchmarks. As shared in our article “**[Fable 5.2 Advances the Frontier](https://patmcguinness.substack.com/p/fable-52-advances-the-frontier),**” Fable 5.2 is most important for its new long-horizon capabilities: Claude Fable 5.2 can generate full robust end-to-end software autonomously, solve major theoretical physics problems, create videos, and design electronic hardware using CAD. Mythos 5.2 is only available to selected trusted users for cyber defense, while Fable 5.2 is available to Claude subscribers and via API. Priced at $8 / $40 per million input/ output tokens, Fable 5.2 is 20% cheaper per token than Fable 5.1 but can be costly to run on extended tasks because it thinks longer to obtain its best results. It has four thinking levels and a 1 million token context window, and scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at default high thinking (and 54 at xhigh). With improved intelligence benchmarks similar to frontier mid-range AI models Claude Sonnet 5.5 or GPT-6.1 Terra, Google presents Hydrogen as a work-horse for agentic tasks: > ***Hydrogen is built to stand on its own as a model for everyday work - or to pair with Carbon and Argon as the high-efficiency execution engine in multi-model workflows.*** To support this, **[Google has integrated it into Google Antigravity alongside a multi-model Orchestrator](https://antigravity.google/blog/gemini-4-hydrogen-in-google-antigravity)** so that complex coding tasks can be done more efficiently combining Carbon and Hydrogen AI models on tasks. [Gemini 4 Hydrogen is 2.5 times faster](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-hydrogen/) than and is priced similarly to its predecessor Gemini 3.8 Flash at $1.50 / $7.50 per million input / output tokens. **[Google released its new frontier model Gemini 4 Carbon](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/gemini-4-carbon-now-available/?utm_source=deepmind.google&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=gdm&utm_content=)** to general availability, two weeks after the limited launch to cybersecurity defenders. Gemini 4 Carbon is available via paid Gemini API at an introductory price of $2/$10 per million input/output tokens and through Google AI Ultra subscriptions. On November 12, 2026, researchers from Shanghai AI Laboratory, East China Normal University, Fudan University, and Shanghai Jiao Tong University released the ArchSpace preprint on arXiv, introducing an open-source evaluation framework and collaborative registry designed to systematically record, review, and reference large language model architectural designs. ## Addressing the Industry-Academia Divide in LLM Architecture Research The design of a large language model architecture directly dictates its training throughput, inference efficiency, and downstream task performance. In an arXiv [preprint](/dictionary/term/preprint) titled ‘ArchSpace: Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing LLM Architecture Research’ (arXiv:2611.17332), lead author Jie Wang and colleagues highlight a widening imbalance in how architectural advances are documented and disseminated across the machine learning community. While leading industrial laboratories—including teams behind open-weight model families such as DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi—frequently incorporate novel architectural components into production models, public technical reports rarely document the iterative search process, the architectural alternatives explored, or the specific design choices that failed. Conversely, academic research groups face acute computational limitations that often restrict architectural experiments to small model scales and disparate training baselines. On November 11, 2026, Amazon Web Services released the Universal Agent Evaluation Framework (UAEF), an open-source, framework-agnostic evaluation system designed to benchmark and track autonomous artificial intelligence agents across their development lifecycle. Published by researchers from the AWS Forward Deployed Engineer team, the system introduces a standardized method for converting disparate agent traces into a canonical execution representation, enabling direct behavioral comparison across frameworks such as LangGraph, LangChain, and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. By uniting 36 built-in metrics across seven operational dimensions with automated regression detection, the framework establishes a repeatable methodology for evaluating multi-turn reasoning and tool invocation in complex computational pipelines. ## Normalizing Agent Traces Across Heterogeneous Frameworks Modern agentic workflows in academic and enterprise settings rely on a heterogeneous assortment of orchestration libraries. The round, led by CapitalG with participation from GIC, DFJ Growth, IVP, and Sapphire Ventures, more than doubles the company’s reported valuation from roughly a year ago. The bigger story is where LangChain is choosing to compete. The company began as an open-source project that helped early large language models search the web, call APIs, and interact with databases. As frontier AI companies built those capabilities directly into their own systems, LangChain moved up the stack. Its focus is now the creation, deployment, and management of AI agents through LangSmith. Advertisement ## The valuable layer is shifting from models to management That change says something important about the AI market. The basic skills that made early language models difficult to use are becoming standard features. The commercial opportunity is moving toward the layer that helps businesses decide how agents behave, which tools they can access, how they are monitored, and where responsibility sits when something goes wrong. LangChain’s pitch is deliberately platform-neutral. TechCrunch reports that LangSmith is designed to avoid locking customers into a particular model, cloud, or AI ecosystem. That position matters because businesses are increasingly likely to use several models at once, whether for cost, performance, privacy, or redundancy. It also reflects a more practical phase of enterprise AI adoption. Companies do not just need an impressive model. They need a way to make an agent useful inside existing systems without handing their entire operating environment to one cloud provider or frontier lab. The control layer becomes the product. ## Why the valuation is a bet on operational trust LangChain reportedly now has 7,000 LangSmith customers, including Harvey, Rippling, Clay, Nvidia, Toyota, and Salesforce. Those names do not prove that agent adoption has become routine, but they show the kind of customer base the category is chasing: companies that need AI systems to work across real workflows rather than inside isolated demonstrations. On November 12, 2026, researchers from Northeastern University, Parallax, the University of Copenhagen, and the University of Oxford released an arXiv preprint demonstrating that transformer large language models represent explicit, causal task goals in a sparse subset of internal attention heads. Led by Arnab Sen Sharma and David Bau, the study isolates how autoregressive models formulate multi-step plans and verbalize upcoming sub-goals prior to token emission, offering critical empirical evidence for mechanistic interpretability and safety auditing across advanced AI systems. ## Preprint Overview: Tracing Internal Goal Representations The preprint, titled ‘Goal Encoding in LLMs’ (arXiv:2611.17297), addresses a central unresolved debate in artificial intelligence: whether the goal-directed behavior displayed by language models reflects genuine internal intent representations or merely surface-level statistical mimicry. Grounding their inquiry in philosophical planning frameworks, the research team defines a goal as a functional internal state exhibiting three specific properties: pre-commitment prior to action execution, plasticity across diverse realization environments, and temporal persistence throughout execution. As an unreviewed preprint hosted on the [arXiv computer science repository](/guides/arxiv-computer-science), the manuscript has not yet undergone formal peer review. When a generation fails, evaluators cannot readily determine whether the model lacked visual design capabilities or failed to coordinate the spatio-temporal physics of the requested movement. Common anomalies include objects spontaneously vanishing or multiplying, unnatural trajectories unaligned with gravity or inertia, distorted fluid dynamics, and synthetic slow-motion artifacts during high-energy collisions. While human viewers quickly identify these physical impossibilities, video generation systems lack intrinsic mechanisms to distinguish between visual photorealism and causal consistency. Resolving this gap through empirical training data presents severe logistical barriers. Capturing physical events—such as a glass tumbling and shattering upon impact—requires extensive physical laboratory apparatus to systematically vary drop heights, collision angles, and surface materials. AI Product.content: ![BIOENGINEER.ORG](https://bioengineer.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/09/logo_sariyazi.png) ![Bioengineer.org](https://bioengineer.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/11/logo352-e1516556386659.png) # Arda Launches AI Software to Accelerate Manufacturing Assembly Plans for American Factories ![](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/?s=80&r=g) ![Arda Launches AI Software to Accelerate Manufacturing Assembly Plans for American Factories](https://bioengineer.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/stackrss-featured-12215-750x422-bio-45291705a30e-750w.webp) Arda Launches AI Software to Accelerate Manufacturing Assembly Plans for American Factories A new artificial intelligence company named Arda launched in October 2026 with the goal of helping American factories transition products from the design phase to physical production more rapidly. The enterprise is engineering specialized artificial intelligence software engineered to translate product designs directly into operational assembly plans. In addition to generating initial production roadmaps, the platform dynamically updates these assembly instructions whenever underlying product designs undergo revisions. The underlying software technology aims to assist industrial manufacturers in adjusting their production operations with greater speed, significantly compressing the conventional turnaround time between engineering a concept and fabricating the final product. Operating under the leadership of former OpenAI chief research officer Bob McGrew, Arda has secured $232 million in capital funding and reached an overall market valuation of $1.5 billion. The company has announced strategic plans to expand its core technology into robotic assembly operations, aiming to deploy models that allow automated production lines to configure to new designs within days rather than months. Among Arda’s founding researchers is 2024 Hertz Fellow Owen Dugan, who joined the startup in January as its initial artificial intelligence hire. During his opening weeks working with the organization, Dugan developed a functional prototype demonstration that subsequently served as the foundation for Arda’s debut commercial product offering. Dugan stated that his decision to join the enterprise was driven by a commitment to helping American manufacturing facilities build at a faster pace. He noted that receiving the Hertz Fellowship provided him with the autonomy to take a professional risk on an early-stage company and reinforced the conviction that ambitious ideas warrant pursuit. Dugan emphasized that strengthening domestic manufacturing capabilities is an avenue through which he hopes to uphold the fellows’ collective moral commitment to aid the nation in times of need. Alongside his engineering efforts in factory software, Dugan is slated to present his academic artificial intelligence research at the NeurIPS 2026 conference in Sydney. His accepted scientific work outlines a theoretical and operational framework for jointly training incrementally refinable Transformer widths utilizing restart-free adaptive inference mechanisms. Dugan’s broader computational portfolio includes granted patents for algorithmic systems that eliminate satellite trails from astronomical exposures, tackling an expanding data disruption confronted by astronomers as commercial satellite constellations multiply in orbit. Furthermore, Dugan previously co-founded an independent startup focused on verifying the provenance and authenticity of digital images. He now applies this practical computational background at Arda, collaborating alongside researchers and software engineers hailing from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Palantir, and Tesla to advance AI-driven manufacturing tools. Dugan was one of 18 doctoral researchers chosen for the Hertz Fellowship in 2024, recognized as the nation’s most competitive doctoral fellowship within applied sciences, engineering, and mathematics. AI Product.content: # Adobe’s Next Decade Depends on Being Everywhere Creative Work Happens ### Adobe wants to serve creatives who embrace AI and those who want nothing to do with it, betting that however an idea starts, the work that matters will still be finished in Adobe’s tools [Ken Yeung](https://substack.com/@thekenyeung) An AI-generated photo of a bus shelter on the street in Miami Beach displaying an ad for Adobe MAX. Credit: Adobe Firefly/Ken Yeung Adobe has a message for creatives wondering whether it can keep up: Don’t count it out. With Figma, Canva, and a wave of AI-first upstarts competing for their attention, the company insists that Creative Cloud has always been more than a collection of desktop apps. It’s a platform built on trust, security, and more than four decades of experience. “Creative Cloud is the assurance that the technology we provide isn’t going anywhere,” [Deepa Subramaniam](https://www.linkedin.com/in/iamdeepa/), Adobe’s vice president of product marketing for creative professionals, said, vowing that Adobe would continue to be there for creatives “next week, next year, and next decade.” That promise came as Adobe held its annual MAX conference this month while also navigating a [leadership transition](https://theaieconomy.substack.com/p/adobe-fourth-chapter-anil-chakravarthy-ceo). It’s also added new editing capabilities to Photoshop, Premiere, and InDesign; expanded Firefly into what [Mike Polner](https://www.linkedin.com/in/mikepolner/), Adobe’s vice president of product marketing for creators, describes as an AI creative studio “built for every creator”; and given enterprise marketing teams a new way to [coordinate AI agents through GenStudio](https://thelettertwo.com/2026/11/10/adobe-cx-experience-coworker-genstudio-max-2026/). Taken together, Adobe’s MAX announcements made a broader argument than what any single product possibly could. The company wants its tools wherever creative work happens, whether that’s inside its own apps, through a chatbot like ChatGPT, Claude, or Copilot, or with an AI agent a creator already relies on. AI Product.content: [Artificial Intelligence](/category/artificial-intelligence) # Grok Bots get phones, cards and Slack seats Grok Bot ships AI teammates with their own logins in seven weeks, forcing a rethink of permissions. ![StartupHub.ai Staff](https://cdn.startuphub.ai/storage/v1/object/public/avatars/armFile7DFy4_favicon.jpg) By StartupHub.ai Staff, reviewed by [Daniel Singer](/author/daniel-singer), Editor ·2 min read Grok Bots get phones, cards and Slack seatsStartupHub.ai Staff · Nov 14, 2026 · 2 min read Lauren Tan and Roman Ugarte, the engineers who took Grok Bot from first code to launch, told [Y Combinator](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JpJUHOe8bDo) what the product does. It creates AI teammates with their own identity, phone number, credit card and computer, Ugarte said. Those teammates work in Slack, X DMs, email, meetings and ad accounts. No attack was demoed and no remote access was needed. The risk they described was local: too much permission and unclear orders. Seven weeks is the number to hold. ![Grok Bot: What Changes When You Can Build AI Teammates - YC](https://img.youtube.com/vi/JpJUHOe8bDo/maxresdefault.jpg) Grok Bot: What Changes When You Can Build AI Teammates, YC Ugarte said the team went from first line of code to internal launch in seven weeks, after seeing long-running coding agents change engineering work. The question was what that pattern looks like for non-engineers. About two weeks before the talk, Ugarte said, the team shipped Team Bots for sharing one bot across a company. Speed of build versus speed of sharing is the comparison: a quick prototype, then a quick move to multi-user control. Tan said she still uses Cursor for coding but keeps Grok Bot for the outer loop, pulling context from Slack threads and tagging bots where work happens. Ugarte said performance marketing gave its bot logins for [Google](https://www.startuphub.ai/ai-news/artificial-intelligence/2026/apple-s-ai-push-siri-s-overhaul-and-chip-deals) Ads and Facebook Ads plus a budget to test assets with the design bot. That is different from single-player coding and closer to Moltbook-style swarms discussed in the talk, where bots trade messages without a human in the room. On access, Ugarte said the rule is to treat a bot like a new hire with scoped credentials that expand with trust. Tan said each bot has an owner and manager with collaborators invited. Docs for Team Bots add a check not detailed in the talk: what a bot learns for the whole team waits for owner or Manager approval under Review learnings and nothing personal is saved for the team, per [xAI docs](https://docs.x.ai/grok-bot/team-bots). The figures say nothing about how many bots hold spend power or how often approvals fail. Published audit logs of bot actions and grants would change the read. Small firms that cannot hire are early testers, trading hiring pain for delegation risk. If a bot holds its own logins and talks to other bots overnight, who signs off before money moves? [Signup](/reader/signup) ![ad_close_btn](/static/images/svg%20icons/cross_svg.svg) Powered by : # OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Wallet, Lets AI Agents Make Purchases ## ChatGPT Wallet brings AI agents into online checkout, combining biometric approval, secure card tokens and existing payment systems for eligible US users. ![author-image](https://img-cdn.publive.online/fit-in/100x0/filters:format(webp)/ciol/media/member_avatars/2026/04/22/2026-04-22t055912587z-whatsapp-image-2026-04-21-at-50335-pm-2026-04-22-11-26-32.jpeg ) ![](/static/images/google_news.png) Follow Us ![](/static/images/google_news.png) ![IMG_6103](https://img-cdn.publive.online/fit-in/1280x960/filters:format(webp)/ciol/media/media_files/2026/11/14/chatgpt-wallet-2026-11-14-21-55-26.png) OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT Wallet, a new payment feature that allows AI agents to make purchases on behalf of users while keeping their actual card details hidden from the agent and merchant. Announced on November 13, 2026, the wallet has been developed in partnership with American Express, Mastercard and Visa. It is initially rolling out through OpenAI's dots personal agent to eligible ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the United States. The launch takes OpenAI further into online commerce, where AI is moving from helping people find products and compare options to participating in the actual purchase process. But the company is taking a cautious approach. For now, users must review and approve every transaction through a security check, such as Face ID or fingerprint authentication. The requirement shows one of the biggest challenges in AI-led commerce: allowing software to act on someone's behalf without giving it unrestricted control over their money. ## How ChatGPT Wallet Works ChatGPT Wallet is designed to let users save an eligible payment card once and use it for subsequent purchases without repeatedly entering their card information. When an AI agent is ready to complete a purchase, it presents the merchant, selected items, total amount and payment card for the customer to review. The transaction cannot proceed until the user approves it through biometric authentication or another supported security check. After approval, the payment network generates a token containing substitute payment credentials, including a card number, expiration date and security code. The merchant processes the payment using these credentials instead of receiving the customer's actual card details. This arrangement is intended to keep sensitive card information out of the AI agent's reach while allowing purchases to move through existing payment systems. It also preserves the customer's existing card rewards and applicable protections for eligible disputes, including situations involving defective products. Importantly, approving a transaction does not automatically mean an order has been successfully placed. Users still need confirmation from the merchant that the purchase has been completed. ## Why OpenAI Is Entering Payments Online shopping has become a significant part of how people use AI assistants. Consumers increasingly turn to conversational tools to research products, understand specifications and compare alternatives before deciding what to buy. The model does occasionally confuse similar-looking objects, though, and it can't yet reliably plan complex action sequences on its own. **AI company Runway has released its robot model Praxis-1 with open weights and source code. The model uses what it learned from video to control robots and shows promising results in the company's own tests.** Runway has released Praxis-1, its AI model for controlling robots. The company first introduced Praxis-1 in late September but initially gave access only to select partners. Alongside the release, Runway published a detailed research report with new performance tests. Runway's model weights and source code are available under the Apache 2.0 license, which allows commercial use. Ad Praxis-1 takes in camera images, text instructions, and information about a robot's position. From those inputs, it predicts how the environment will change and calculates the right robot movements. As new camera frames come in, the model continuously adjusts its control. Ad ## Praxis-1 builds on video training to control robots Praxis-1 builds on a video model that learned how objects move and interact from ordinary footage. Runway then fine-tuned it with videos of human actions and robot data. This approach could reduce the need for expensive robot-specific datasets, which have traditionally been collected just to train these kinds of systems. Runway is best known for generative video models like [Gen-4.5](https://the-decoder.de/runway-gen-4-5-beansprucht-benchmark-fuehrung-vor-sora-und-veo/). With Praxis-1, the company is bringing its video research into robotics. Runway calls Praxis-1 a [World Action Model](https://the-decoder.de/world-action-models-forscher-kartieren-das-naechste-paradigma-der-robotik-ki/) that predicts how a scene will change and derives matching robot movements from those predictions. Since September, robotics companies Standard Bots, Noble Machines, and Ultra have been testing Praxis-1 on different systems, including a humanoid robot, an industrial robot arm, and a dual-arm warehouse robot. Ad ## Praxis-1 leads among World Action Models Praxis-1 still needs some specialized robot data. To adapt it to a Franka robot arm, Runway used about 277 hours of recordings from the public DROID research dataset, according to its [research report](https://runway.com/research/praxis-1-video-pretraining-to-robot-control). On November 12, 2026, artificial intelligence research laboratory Zyphra publicly released ZONOS3-Mini, an open-source text-to-speech and zero-shot voice cloning model featuring 100 million active parameters under a permissive Apache 2.0 license. The release combines real-time on-device audio generation with fine-grained vocal controllability across 43 languages, providing academic laboratories with an open-weights alternative to proprietary commercial speech APIs. ## Architecture and Inference Efficiency ZONOS3-Mini addresses the persistent tension in neural speech synthesis between acoustic fidelity and computational cost. While previous foundation speech models relied on multi-billion parameter backbones operating over high-frequency audio representations, ZONOS3-Mini adopts a sparse Latent Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture with 800 million total parameters that routes tokens across 64 experts to activate only approximately 100 million parameters per forward pass. The sequence modeling backbone utilizes an 11-layer hybrid architecture designated `gdn3_global1`, configured with a hidden dimension of 1,024. The layer stack combines 9 Gated DeltaNet (GDN) linear recurrent layers with 2 global Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) layers featuring 16 query heads and 4 key-value heads. Operating with Full Attention Residuals across a 32,768-token context window, the model can synthesize up to 10 minutes of continuous speech while maintaining constant memory scaling during linear recurrent generation. According to Zyphra’s published benchmarks, the model was pre-trained in 2.5 days on a cluster of 112 NVIDIA H100 GPUs. In deployment, ZONOS3-Mini achieves a median time-to-first-audio (TTFA) of 80 milliseconds on a single NVIDIA H100, reaching peak throughput of 457 seconds of audio generated per second of wall-clock time. On edge hardware, the architecture achieves a TTFA under 150 milliseconds on an Apple Silicon M3 MacBook Air and under 570 milliseconds running purely in-browser via WebGPU on a Google Pixel 9. ## Acoustic Codec and Mechanistic Vocal Control A central technical advancement in ZONOS3-Mini is the Zyphra Audio Codec 1 (ZAC-1). Open Source AI.content: * [About](/about) * [Advertisement](/advertisement) * [Login / Join](/login) News # Alibaba's Open Code Review Gains Momentum on GitHub with 51,009 Stars Alibaba's Open Code Review, a hybrid AI-powered code review tool, reaches 51,009 stars on GitHub, showcasing scalability and precision. [Felix Pinkston](/Profile/Felix-Pinkston) [![Alibaba's Open Code Review Gains Momentum on GitHub with 51,009 Stars](https://image.blockchain.news:443/features/24B6EBDC6093F0C1F639A6A7DA12473E2D2C5C390185833B0F398CC7FCE1368C.jpg)](https://image.blockchain.news:443/features/24B6EBDC6093F0C1F639A6A7DA12473E2D2C5C390185833B0F398CC7FCE1368C.jpg) On November 14, 2026, Alibaba's open-source project **Open Code Review** surged on GitHub Trending, gaining 897 stars in a single day to reach a total of 51,009 stars and 3,804 forks. Written primarily in Go, this hybrid AI-powered code review tool has been described as secure, fast, efficient, and battle-tested at Alibaba's scale. ## Technical Features and Capabilities Open Code Review combines deterministic pipelines with an LLM (large language model) agent to deliver precise line-level comments during code reviews. It includes a built-in multi-language ruleset addressing issues such as null pointer exceptions (NPE), thread-safety, cross-site scripting (XSS), and SQL injection vulnerabilities. The tool is compatible with OpenAI and Anthropic models, providing flexibility for developers to configure their preferred model endpoints. The tool supports both diff-based reviews for pull requests and full-file scans for auditing unfamiliar codebases. By leveraging its hybrid architecture, Open Code Review balances deterministic engineering with the contextual understanding of an LLM agent, ensuring both precision and depth in its analysis. ## Benchmark Performance According to benchmarks conducted on a dataset of 50 popular open-source repositories, 200 real pull requests, and 10 programming languages, Open Code Review demonstrated significantly higher precision and F1 scores compared to general-purpose agents like Claude Code. Notably, it achieved these results while consuming only about one-ninth of the tokens and completing reviews faster. However, its recall was intentionally lower, prioritizing precision to reduce false positives. The benchmark dataset, known as AACR-Bench, was cross-validated by over 80 senior engineers and included 1,505 annotated ground-truth issues. Metrics such as precision, recall, F1 score, average review time, and token consumption were evaluated to highlight the tool's efficiency and cost-effectiveness. ## Adoption and Practical Use Initially developed as an internal tool at Alibaba, Open Code Review has identified millions of code defects over two years of use by tens of thousands of developers. Its open-source release aims to benefit the broader developer community. Installation is straightforward via npm, and the tool integrates seamlessly with Git for diff generation and repository operations. Developers can use commands like `ocr review` for pull request reviews or `ocr scan` for full-file audits. As of November 14, 2026, the repository is licensed under Apache License 2.0 and continues to gain traction among developers worldwide. For more details, users can visit the project's official website at [open-codereview.ai](https://open-codereview.ai). * [alibaba](/tag/alibaba) * [open-source](/tag/open-source) * [ai](/tag/ai) * [github](/tag/github) * [code review](/tag/code-review) [Sign in to save this article](/login?lang=en&returnUrl=%2Fnews%2Falibaba-open-code-review-github-trending) Free account: build your research collection and return to read it anytime. The update gives applications using V4.1-Flash access to hosted web search, document parsing, URL reading, and content safety checks. DeepSeek also offers separate services for extracting text and working with speech. The company published a working chat demo and opened its source code so developers can see how the pieces fit together. The change is easy to picture if you’ve ever asked a chatbot to read a PDF and then look up something the PDF leaves out. Those actions feel like part of one conversation. Behind the scenes, they can take several integrations. DeepSeek is now offering developers a way to put those actions into their own apps using the same service. ## What changed for V4.1-Flash [DeepSeek](https://kingy.ai/blog/deepseek-federal-ban-local-ai-private-users/) identifies `deepseek-flash` as the model to use for the new conversation features. Developers can access them through three API formats: Messages, Responses, and Chat Completions. DeepSeek’s service runs the built-in tools and assembles the context the model needs. Its guide explains how the client displays returned content and carries it forward in a conversation. [DeepSeek’s chatbot developer guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/build_a_chatbot/) That arrangement can save a team from writing code to coordinate a search, retrieve a page, and pass the relevant material to the model. The app still needs to make that work legible. A reader should be able to tell which sources informed an answer, and a developer should be able to tell where a request stalled when something goes wrong. ## Web search arrives with citations With the web tool enabled and thinking mode off, V4.1-Flash can decide when to search the web or look for images and include citations in its answer. An app can display those citations alongside the reply. For a question about a recently updated product or policy, the links give users a way to see where the information came from. Picture a small business owner asking when applications for a local grant close. A helpful answer gives the date and points to the program page. If that page describes last year’s grant, the answer can still be wrong. Showing the citation makes that easier to spot. For an app that handles questions like this regularly, the quality of the link matters almost as much as the clarity of the answer. ## Deep thinking search can follow a trail [DeepSeek](https://kingy.ai/news/deepseek-search-fetch-apis-pricing-features/) also offers a search mode that works during multi-step reasoning. With thinking mode and the search tool enabled, the model can search, read pages, and take additional steps based on what it finds. Infra & Chips.content: [![Foreign Policy Journal](https://foreignpolicyjournal.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/09/FPJ-logo-bw-globe-banner.png)](https://www.foreignpolicyjournal.com/) * [Home](https://foreignpolicyjournal.com/) * [Politics](https://www.foreignpolicyjournal.com/category/politics/) * [Economy & Business](https://www.foreignpolicyjournal.com/category/economy/) * [US News](https://www.foreignpolicyjournal.com/category/features/news-analysis/) * [Energy](https://www.foreignpolicyjournal.com/category/energy/) Select Page # AI Data Center Stocks Crater On Nebius Outlook And Nvidia Uncertainty, But Applied Digital’s (NASDAQ: APLD) $36.2B Lease Book Remains Intact By [David Prior](https://www.foreignpolicyjournal.com/author/davidprior/ "Posts by David Prior") | Nov 14, 2026 | [Economy & Business](https://www.foreignpolicyjournal.com/category/economy/), [Featured](https://www.foreignpolicyjournal.com/category/featured/), [News & Analysis](https://www.foreignpolicyjournal.com/category/features/news-analysis/) ![AI Data Center Stocks Crater On Nebius Outlook And Nvidia Uncertainty, But Applied Digital’s (NASDAQ: APLD) $36.2B Lease Book Remains Intact](https://www.foreignpolicyjournal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/Applied-Digital-Corporation-1280x640.webp) A $36.2 billion portfolio of signed, non-cancellable leases did nothing to shield Applied Digital (NASDAQ: APLD) from a brutal morning session, as shares slid 10% despite zero company-specific news. The selloff swept across the AI infrastructure sector, with Nebius (NASDAQ: NBIS) dropping 13%, CoreWeave (NASDAQ: CRWV) losing roughly 10%, IREN (NASDAQ: IREN) shedding 10%, and Cipher Digital (NASDAQ: CIFR) falling 9%. The catalyst was Nebius, whose third-quarter revenue surged 571% to $980.8 million but included $325.1 million in non-recurring strategic partnership payments that raised quality-of-earnings questions. Bank of America flagged that Nebius’s guidance implies a sequential revenue decline in the fourth quarter, with delays at third-party data centers pushing recognized revenue into early 2027. A separate and arguably more alarming disclosure was a $40 billion capital spending plan for 2027, which rattled investors already sensitive to the pace of AI infrastructure buildout. Nvidia’s leadership transition compounded the anxiety, as The Information reported that the chipmaker is expected to pull back on AI investments and credit guarantees following Jensen Huang’s exit as CEO on Thursday. That report hit IREN particularly hard, given that Nvidia represents a $3.4 billion customer relationship for the company, while Cipher fell alongside news from the Wall Street Journal that private neocloud Nscale requires additional financing before its planned IPO. None of these developments altered a single dollar of Applied Digital’s contracted revenue, where two anchor tenants account for 86% of the total signed lease value: a tier-one hyperscaler holding $20.2 billion and CoreWeave holding $11 billion across 15-year agreements. CoreWeave’s own financial position draws scrutiny, with its bonds yielding above 17%, yet the leases carry no cancellation provisions and CoreWeave pays approximately 10% more per megawatt than hyperscaler peers. Wall Street expects Applied Digital’s revenue to more than triple between fiscal 2026 and fiscal 2028, with minimum lease payments alone projected to reach $1.58 billion in fiscal 2028, representing around 80% of that year’s consensus estimate. At today’s depressed price, Applied Digital trades at well under 5x forward sales, compared to a three-year average multiple of roughly 11x, a gap that suggests the market is pricing in risks beyond what the contracted backlog justifies. The genuine vulnerability is not the tenants but the capital required to bring additional capacity online: CEO Wes Cummins stated this month that the company must still finance approximately 800 MW over the coming 12 months. Infra & Chips.title: Microsoft Winds Down Oracle AI Cloud Deal As Older NVIDIA GPUs No Longer Meet Its Needs
Infra & Chips.titleZh: Microsoft Winds Down Oracle AI Cloud Deal As Older NVIDIA GPUs No Longer Meet Its Needs
Infra & Chips.content: # Microsoft Winds Down Oracle AI Cloud Deal As Older NVIDIA GPUs No Longer Meet Its Needs [Sebastian Castellanos](https://wccftech.com/author/sebastian/) • [Comments](#comments "View comments") [![](https://www.gstatic.com/images/branding/productlogos/googleg_gradient/v1/24px.svg) Add to Preferred Sources](javascript:void(0)) Microsoft is reportedly **winding down its AI computing agreement with Oracle**, after deciding that the older-generation NVIDIA GPUs powering the rented infrastructure no longer meet its evolving requirements. The move raises further questions about the long-term economics of AI data centers, particularly as technology companies continue pouring billions into increasingly expensive hardware. According to a [**November 6 report from Bloomberg**](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-11-06/microsoft-is-winding-down-oracle-deal-to-rent-ai-cloud-capacity), citing people familiar with the matter, Microsoft declined to renew its contract with Oracle and has gradually been switching off the rented computing capacity over recent months. [##### **Related Story** GeForce RTX 5090 And RTX 5080 Witness A Sudden Price Drop Of Up To 22% In Japan, But It’s Unlikely Due To Jensen’s Resignation](https://wccftech.com/geforce-rtx-5090-and-rtx-5080-witness-a-sudden-price-drop-of-up-to-22-in-japan-but-its-unlikely-due-to-jensens-resignation/) The agreement dates back to November 2023, when [**Oracle announced**](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/oracle-cloud-infrastructure-utilized-by-microsoft-for-bing-conversational-search-301979431.html) that Microsoft would leverage **Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI)** alongside **Azure** to provide AI inference capabilities for **Bing's conversational search engine**. At the time, demand for AI accelerators was outpacing available supply, forcing even major cloud providers to seek computing resources from competitors. However, Microsoft's requirements have since changed, and the older NVIDIA accelerators deployed in Oracle's infrastructure reportedly no longer meet its specifications. **Neither the exact GPU models involved nor the financial value of the agreement has been disclosed**. [![A presentation slide titled 'ANNOUNCING' displays 'Oracle Cloud Infrastructure' featuring NVIDIA models P100, V100, A100, H100, H200, GB200, GB300, AMD models MI300x, MI355x, M1455x, and other technologies from Google, Positron, Broadcom, Cerebras, and SambaNova.](https://cdn.wccftech.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Oracle-Cloud-AI-scaled-1.jpg)](https://cdn.wccftech.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Oracle-Cloud-AI-scaled-1.jpg) *Oracle is expanding its cloud infrastructure with next-generation NVIDIA, AMD, and other AI accelerators, even as Microsoft winds down its older AI computing agreement. Image credit: Wccftech.* ## Oracle Insists Older GPUs Remain Valuable Oracle has pushed back against suggestions that aging AI hardware is becoming commercially unviable, maintaining that demand for its infrastructure remains strong. In a [**statement reported by Reuters**](https://www.reuters.com/business/microsoft-is-winding-down-oracle-deal-rent-ai-cloud-capacity-bloomberg-news-2026-11-06/), an Oracle spokesperson emphasized that demand remains robust even for previous-generation GPUs. The company also revealed that during its first quarter of fiscal 2027, **GPU capacity coming up for renewal was renewed or resold at a 20% premium over previous contract prices**, despite most of those accelerators being at least four years old. Oracle reported GPU utilization of approximately 97.9% during the same period. This suggests that while older accelerators might no longer satisfy Microsoft's latest AI requirements, they can remain commercially viable for other customers and workloads. ASML and Nvidia sit at opposite ends of the chip supply chain, and their valuations tell very different stories for investors weighing new money. By[Seena Hassouna](/author/20695/) – Updated Nov 14, 2026 at 4:54PM EST [+Fool.comon](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=fool.com) ## Key Points * ASML is the sole provider of the advanced lithography machines required to manufacture the world's most sophisticated semiconductors. * Nvidia dominates the market for high-performance graphics processors that power artificial intelligence and accelerated computing. * Which semiconductor stock deserves a spot in your portfolio? Can the company that builds the machines to make chips outpace the company that designs the chips themselves? Here is how to choose between **ASML** ([ASML](/quote/nasdaq/asml/) -0.13%) and **Nvidia** ([NVDA](/quote/nasdaq/nvda/) -2.01%) for your portfolio. ASML provides the critical lithography equipment used by every major chipmaker to etch tiny circuits onto silicon wafers. Nvidia is the leader in graphics processing units (GPUs) that have become the standard for training massive artificial intelligence models. These two giants are essential to the global tech ecosystem, making them top considerations for any investor. ## The case for ASML ASML sells lithography machines that use light to print circuit patterns on wafers. It has a near-monopoly on Extreme Ultraviolet (EUV) systems, which are necessary for the world's smallest and most powerful chips. These systems are incredibly complex, often requiring dozens of freight planes to transport a single machine and costing hundreds of millions of dollars each for high-end models. In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $43.6 billion, representing growth of roughly 22.5% compared to the prior year. During this same period, the company generated net income of approximately $14.9 billion. Growth was driven by strong demand in both the logic and memory markets as global chipmakers ramped up production for artificial intelligence applications. As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was roughly 0.2x, which compares total debt to the value of assets owned by stockholders.
